title: Pericyte loss and endothelial activation define distinct vascular states in cerebral small vessel disease
title_zh: 周细胞缺失与内皮激活定义大脑小血管疾病中的不同血管状态
abstract: Abstract Cerebral small vessel disease (cSVD) is a leading cause of stroke and vascular cognitive impairment, yet the cellular mechanisms underlying microvascular dysfunction in human disease remain incompletely understood. In particular, the relationship between pericyte alterations and endothelial activation, two key features of blood–brain barrier dysfunction, remains unresolved. Here, we performed a quantitative single-vessel analysis of the human cortical microvasculature across increasing cSVD severity and ageing. Using multiplex immunohistochemistry combined with spectral unmixing and automated image analysis, we analysed 11,409 microvascular fragments from post-mortem brain tissue derived from 20 cases. Endothelial cells, pericytes, and endothelial activation were assessed using PECAM-1, PDGFRβ, and VCAM-1, respectively. Microvascular density and diameter differed between cortical grey matter and the underlying white matter, with white matter vessels being less dense and wider in controls. While vessel diameter remained stable across cSVD severity groups, microvascular density increased with cSVD severity and age in the white matter. At the molecular level, PDGFRβ signal decreased markedly with increasing cSVD severity, consistent with reduced pericyte coverage. This reduction was observed in both grey and white matter and correlated with disease severity and age. Notably, intermediate severity groups displayed marked heterogeneity, with vessels exhibiting either preserved or markedly reduced PDGFRβ signal. In parallel, endothelial markers PECAM-1 and VCAM-1 increased significantly with disease severity, reflecting endothelial activation. Unsupervised Gaussian mixture clustering of marker expression identified three vascular states characterised by (i) preserved PDGFRβ signal with low endothelial activation, (ii) reduced PDGFRβ signal without endothelial activation, and (iii) reduced PDGFRβ signal combined with endothelial activation. These clusters broadly aligned with neuropathological severity but revealed heterogeneity not captured by post-mortem diagnosis alone. Together, these findings suggest that pericyte alterations and endothelial activation are partially dissociated processes in human cSVD and identify distinct microvascular phenotypes across disease severity. These cross-sectional observations provide a framework for future longitudinal and experimental studies to determine their temporal and mechanistic relationships.
abstract_zh: 摘要：大脑小血管疾病（cSVD）是卒中和血管性认知障碍的主要原因，但人类疾病中微血管功能障碍的细胞机制尚未完全阐明。特别是周细胞改变与内皮激活这两种血脑屏障功能障碍的关键特征之间的关系仍未解决。我们对人类皮质微血管在cSVD严重程度和衰老过程中进行定量单血管分析。利用多重免疫组化结合光谱去混和自动图像分析，分析了来自20例尸检脑组织的11,409个微血管碎片。通过PECAM-1、PDGFRβ和VCAM-1分别评估内皮细胞、周细胞和内皮激活。微血管密度和直径在皮质灰质与下层白质之间存在差异，白质血管在对照组中密度较低且直径更宽。血管直径在cSVD严重程度组间保持稳定，而白质微血管密度随cSVD严重程度和年龄增加而升高。在分子水平上，PDGFRβ信号随cSVD严重程度增加显著下降，提示周细胞覆盖减少。该减少在灰质和白质中均有观察到，并与疾病严重程度和年龄相关。值得注意的是，中等严重程度组表现出明显异质性，血管表现为保留或显著降低的PDGFRβ信号。与此同时，内皮标记物PECAM-1和VCAM-1随疾病严重程度显著升高，反映内皮激活。对标记物表达进行无监督高斯混合聚类，识别出三种血管状态：①保留PDGFRβ信号且内皮激活低；②降低PDGFRβ信号但无内皮激活；③降低PDGFRβ信号并伴随内皮激活。这些聚类与神经病理学严重程度大致一致，但揭示了仅凭尸检诊断无法捕捉的异质性。综上所述，这些发现表明周细胞改变与内皮激活在人体cSVD中是部分分离的过程，并在疾病严重程度上识别出不同的微血管表型。这些横断面观察为未来纵向和实验研究提供了框架，以确定它们的时间和机制关系。
